reading.title: Hybrid Working Policy - Extract
paragraphs: 3. Eligibility and working pattern

3.1 Hybrid working is open to all employees who have completed their probationary period and whose role can be carried out remotely without disrupting the service. It is voluntary: nobody can be required to work from home, and a refusal will never count against an employee.

3.2 Eligible employees may work remotely for up to two days a week. The remaining days are spent on site. Each team agrees one anchor day, on which everyone is expected to come into the office, so that meetings and training can take place in person.

3.3 Remote working days are agreed in advance with your line manager and recorded in the HR system. They may be changed at short notice if the needs of the business so require, for example for a client visit, but your manager will give you as much notice as possible.
4. Working hours and availability
4.1 Your working hours do not change when you work from home. You are expected to be reachable during core hours, namely 10.00 am to 12.00 noon and 2.00 pm to 4.00 pm, and to take your usual breaks.

4.2 You are not expected to read or reply to messages outside your working hours. Managers should avoid sending non-urgent emails in the evening or at weekends, and should make clear when a reply can wait.
5. Ending the arrangement
5.1 Either you or the Company may bring the arrangement to an end by giving one month's written notice. You will then return to working on site full-time, at your usual place of work.

Only managers
Employees who have finished their probation and whose job allows it
Employees chosen by the Company, who must then accept
questions.explain_fr: Le point 3.1 pose deux conditions : avoir terminé sa période d'essai et occuper un poste compatible. Le télétravail reste volontaire : personne ne peut y être contraint.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the anchor day?
options: To have the whole team in the office on the same day
To give everyone a day at home
To check that employees are really working
To reduce the cost of office space
questions.explain_fr: « Anchor day » : jour où toute l'équipe vient au bureau, pour que réunions et formations aient lieu « in person ».

questions.q: What does clause 4.2 ask managers to do?
options: To stop sending emails altogether
To answer messages within one hour
To check that employees are online in the evening
To avoid non-urgent emails outside working hours
questions.explain_fr: Les managers doivent éviter les courriels non urgents le soir et le week-end et préciser quand une réponse peut attendre : c'est la traduction pratique du droit à la déconnexion.

questions.q: How can the hybrid arrangement be ended?
options: Only by the Company, immediately
By either side, with one month's written notice
Only by the employee, at any time
By the line manager, by email, the day before
questions.explain_fr: « Either you or the Company » : la faculté est réciproque, moyennant un préavis écrit d'un mois. Notez l'apostrophe de « one month's written notice ».

reading.title: Annual Working-Days Arrangement
paragraphs: 6. WORKING TIME

6.1 In view of the autonomy which the Employee enjoys in organising his or her schedule, and in accordance with the applicable company agreement, the Employee's working time shall be measured in days rather than in hours. The Employee shall work [218] days in each full calendar year, inclusive of the day of solidarity.

6.2 The Employee shall accordingly not be subject to the statutory working week or to the provisions governing overtime. He or she shall nevertheless remain entitled to a daily rest period of eleven consecutive hours and a weekly rest period of thirty-five consecutive hours, which the Company undertakes to respect and to cause to be respected.

6.3 The Employee shall record the days and half-days worked, together with the rest days taken, in the self-reporting tool provided for that purpose. The record shall be reviewed each month by the Employee's line manager.

6.4 The Company shall monitor the Employee's workload on a regular basis. A meeting shall be held at least once a year to discuss the Employee's workload, the organisation of his or her work, the balance between working and private life, and remuneration. Without prejudice to the foregoing, the Employee may at any time alert his or her manager in writing to any difficulty, in which case a meeting shall be held without delay.
6.5 The Employee shall have the right to disconnect from the Company's digital tools during rest periods and leave, on the terms laid down in the company agreement.
6.6 Subject to the written agreement of the Company, the Employee may waive part of his or her rest days in return for an increase in remuneration, within the limits prescribed by law.

In hours per year

questions.explain_fr: « Measured in days rather than in hours » : c'est le principe du forfait jours. Le nombre de jours figure entre crochets car il est fixé par l'accord collectif, dans la limite légale.

questions.q: Which rules continue to apply to the employee under clause 6.2?

Daily and weekly rest periods
The overtime provisions
None of the working time rules
questions.explain_fr: Le salarié au forfait jours échappe à la durée légale et aux heures supplémentaires, mais « shall nevertheless remain entitled to » : les repos quotidien et hebdomadaire restent dus.

questions.q: What must happen at least once a year?
options: A meeting about workload, work organisation, work-life balance and pay
A renegotiation of the company agreement
A medical examination
A review of the number of days by the labour inspector
questions.explain_fr: Clause 6.4 : l'entretien annuel de suivi porte sur la charge de travail, l'organisation du travail, l'articulation vie professionnelle / vie privée et la rémunération.

questions.q: What does clause 6.6 allow?
options: The Company to cancel rest days when it is busy
The employee to take extra rest days without pay
The employee to give up some rest days for more pay, if the Company agrees in writing
The employee to carry rest days over to the next year
questions.explain_fr: « To waive » = renoncer à. Le rachat de jours de repos suppose l'accord écrit de l'employeur et une majoration de la rémunération, dans les limites légales.

reading.title: Overtime in France: what you need to know
paragraphs:
To: Dana Whitfield, VP People, Northlake Software Inc.
From: Claire Morel
Re: Overtime rules for your Lyon support team

You asked whether the Lyon support agents could simply be treated as exempt, as their counterparts in Denver are. The short answer is no: French law has no direct equivalent of exempt status, and the starting point is rather different.

The statutory workweek in France is 35 hours. This is not a ceiling. It is the threshold above which every hour counts as overtime and must be paid at a premium rate set by collective agreement or, failing that, by law. By agreement, the premium may be replaced in whole or in part by time off in lieu. An employee cannot give up these rights, even in writing.

Two limits deserve your attention. First, there are absolute caps on daily and weekly hours, together with minimum daily and weekly rest. Second, each employee has an annual overtime quota; beyond it, additional compensatory rest falls due and the works council must be consulted.

There is one arrangement that resembles exempt status: senior, genuinely autonomous staff may have their time counted in days per year rather than in hours. It requires a collective agreement and the employee's written consent, and it comes with a duty to monitor workload. In my view it would not be appropriate for support agents, who work to a fixed schedule.

Finally, a word on evidence. If an employee claims unpaid overtime, the court will expect the company to produce its own records of hours worked. Reliable time recording is therefore your best protection, and I would suggest we review the current timesheets together before the end of the quarter.

glossary.plain: (US) not entitled to overtime pay
glossary.fr: non éligible aux heures supplémentaires (statut américain)

glossary.plain: the level at which something starts to apply
a higher rate of pay than normal
rest given instead of overtime pay
the yearly number of overtime hours beyond which extra rest is owed
the body of elected employee representatives (the CSE in France)
keeping track of the hours employees work

questions.q: What is the main point of the third paragraph?
options: French employees may not work more than 35 hours
35 hours is the point at which overtime starts, not a maximum
Overtime is always paid in time off
Employees can agree in writing to work unpaid overtime
questions.explain_fr: « This is not a ceiling. It is the threshold... » : les 35 heures sont un seuil de déclenchement, pas un plafond. C'est le malentendu qu'il faut dissiper d'emblée avec un client américain.

questions.q: What happens when an employee goes beyond the annual overtime quota?
options: Extra compensatory rest is owed and the works council must be consulted
The overtime becomes illegal
The employee must stop working until the following year
The employee becomes exempt
questions.explain_fr: Au-delà du contingent, les heures restent possibles mais ouvrent droit à une contrepartie obligatoire en repos (« falls due » = devient exigible) et supposent la consultation du CSE.

questions.q: Why does Claire think counting time in days is unsuitable for the support agents?
options: They have not been with the company long enough
There is no collective agreement in France
They are paid too little
They work to a fixed schedule and are not truly autonomous
questions.explain_fr: Le forfait jours est réservé aux salariés réellement autonomes dans l'organisation de leur emploi du temps ; des agents soumis à un horaire fixe n'y sont pas éligibles.

questions.q: What does Claire recommend doing before the end of the quarter?
options: Reclassifying the agents
Negotiating a new collective agreement
Reviewing the timesheets together
Cutting all overtime
questions.explain_fr: « I would suggest we review the current timesheets together » : en cas de litige, l'employeur doit produire ses propres éléments de décompte, d'où l'importance d'un suivi fiable.

reading.title: Summer leave and days to use up
paragraphs: Subject: Summer leave requests and remaining days - please read
Dear all,
With the summer not far off, I'd like to remind everyone how leave is booked, and to flag one or two deadlines.

Please submit your requests for July and August through the HR portal by Friday 28 March. Your manager will reply within ten working days. Until a request has been approved in the system, please don't book flights or accommodation: where several people in the same team ask for the same weeks, managers may have to stagger leave, and priority will go to colleagues with school-age children and to those who missed out last year.
The office will close for the annual shutdown from Monday 11 to Friday 15 August, so everyone needs to keep five days back for that week.

A word on leave balances. The current leave year ends on 31 May. You can check how many days you have left on the portal's home page. Up to five untaken days may be carried over, provided your manager agrees in writing; anything above that will be lost unless you were unable to take it for reasons beyond your control. If you still have a large balance, please speak to your manager now rather than in May.
Before you go away, don't forget to arrange cover with a colleague, prepare a short handover note, and set an out-of-office reply giving your return date and the name of the person to contact.
If anything is unclear, do drop me a line or come and see me.

Kind regards,
Sophie Bertin
HR Officer

glossary.plain: to draw attention to
days when the office is open (Monday to Friday)
arrange for people to be away at different times
a period when the whole company closes
the twelve months over which leave is counted
transferred to the following year
a short document explaining your current work to the person replacing you
an automatic email saying you are away

legalese.phrase: provided your manager agrees in writing
legalese.plain: only if your manager says yes in writing
for reasons you could do nothing about

questions.q: What should employees avoid doing before their request is approved?
options: Talking to their manager
Booking flights or accommodation
Checking their leave balance
Submitting a second request
questions.explain_fr: Tant que la demande n'est pas validée dans le système, mieux vaut ne rien réserver : les dates peuvent être échelonnées (« staggered ») entre collègues.

questions.q: Who gets priority if several colleagues want the same weeks?
options: The most senior managers
Those who asked first
Nobody: the weeks are shared equally
Parents of school-age children and those who missed out last year
questions.explain_fr: « To miss out » = ne pas avoir obtenu ce que l'on souhaitait. Les critères annoncés sont la situation de famille et l'équité par rapport à l'an dernier.

questions.q: Why must everyone keep five days back?
options: The office closes for a week in August
Five days must be carried over each year
Managers need five days to reply
It is a legal minimum for the summer
questions.explain_fr: « To keep days back » = garder des jours en réserve, ici pour la fermeture annuelle (« annual shutdown ») du 11 au 15 août.

questions.q: What happens to untaken days above the carry-over limit?
options: They are paid automatically
They are added to next year's entitlement
They are normally lost
They are given to a colleague
questions.explain_fr: Au-delà de cinq jours reportés avec accord écrit, les jours sont perdus, sauf si le salarié a été empêché de les prendre (« for reasons beyond your control »).

writing.title: Asking the team to book their summer leave
writing.brief: You are the HR officer. Write to all staff asking them to submit their summer leave requests by 28 March. Mention the August shutdown, the carry-over rule and what to do before going away.
writing.brief_fr: Vous êtes chargé(e) de RH. Écrivez à l'ensemble du personnel pour lui demander de déposer ses demandes de congés d'été avant le 28 mars. Mentionnez la fermeture d'août, la règle de report et les démarches à effectuer avant de partir.

gaps.text: Please ___ your leave requests for July and August by Friday 28 March.
gaps.explain_fr: « To submit a request » : le verbe attendu à l'écrit. « To put in a request » convient à l'oral. Évitez « to pose » ou « to deposit ».

gaps.text: The office will be closed from 11 to 15 August, so please keep five days ___ for that week.
gaps.explain_fr: « To keep something back » = garder en réserve. Verbe à particule simple et très naturel.

gaps.text: Up to five untaken days may be carried ___ to the next leave year.
gaps.explain_fr: « To carry over / carry forward » = reporter sur la période suivante. « To report » est un faux ami.

gaps.text: Requests will be dealt with in the order in ___ they are received.
gaps.explain_fr: « In the order in which they are received » : la préposition précède le relatif dans un registre soigné. « In the order they are received » est aussi correct, mais plus relâché.

gaps.text: Before you go, please arrange ___ with a colleague and leave a handover note.
gaps.explain_fr: « To arrange cover » (UK, indénombrable, sans article) = organiser son remplacement. Aux États-Unis : « coverage ».

gaps.text: If you have any questions, please do not ___ to get in touch.
gaps.explain_fr: « Please do not hesitate to get in touch » : formule de clôture classique, moins raide que « to contact me ».

writing.model:
Subject: Summer leave - requests by 28 March

Dear all,

As summer approaches, I would like to remind you of the arrangements for booking leave.

Please submit your leave requests for July and August by Friday 28 March, using the HR portal. Requests will be dealt with in the order in which they are received, and your manager will reply within ten working days.

The office will be closed from 11 to 15 August, so please keep five days back for that week. Up to five untaken days may be carried over to the next leave year, with your manager's agreement.

Before you go, please arrange cover with a colleague and leave a handover note.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to get in touch.

Kind regards,
Sophie Bertin
HR Officer

commentary.quote: As summer approaches
commentary.note_fr: Entrée en matière légère, typique d'un courriel collectif. « With summer approaching » conviendrait aussi.

commentary.quote: by Friday 28 March
commentary.note_fr: « By » = au plus tard le. Date britannique : jour puis mois, sans virgule ; version américaine : « Friday, March 28 ».

commentary.quote: Requests will be dealt with
commentary.note_fr: Le passif évite de désigner qui traite les demandes ; « to deal with » (UK) devient « to handle » en américain.

commentary.quote: with your manager's agreement
commentary.note_fr: Condition glissée en fin de phrase, sans lourdeur. Plus naturel que « under the condition that your manager agrees ».

commentary.quote: please do not hesitate to get in touch
commentary.note_fr: « To get in touch » adoucit la formule. Les Américains écrivent volontiers « feel free to reach out ».

checklist: Have I given a clear deadline with 'by'?
Is each request softened with 'please'?
Have I used 'leave' as an uncountable noun (no 'leaves')?
Are the dates written consistently in British or American format?
Does the email end with an offer to help?
phrasebank: I would like to remind you of the arrangements for ...
Please submit your requests by ...
Requests will be dealt with in the order in which they are received.
Please keep ... days back for ...
Up to ... days may be carried over.
Before you go, please arrange cover.
Please do not hesitate to get in touch.

writing.title: Turning down leave dates and suggesting others
writing.brief: A team member, Lucas, has asked for the first two weeks of August. Two colleagues are already off then. Reply as his manager: you cannot approve those dates, but you can offer the last two weeks of August or any two weeks in July.
writing.brief_fr: Un collaborateur, Lucas, a demandé les deux premières semaines d'août. Deux collègues sont déjà absents à ces dates. Répondez en tant que manager : vous ne pouvez pas valider ces dates, mais vous proposez les deux dernières semaines d'août ou deux semaines au choix en juillet.

gaps.text: Thank you for your request for leave ___ 4 to 15 August.
gaps.explain_fr: « From 4 to 15 August » : « from ... to ... » pour une période. À l'américaine, on trouve aussi « August 4 through 15 ».

gaps.text: I'm ___ I can't approve those dates, as Inès and Paul are already off that fortnight.
gaps.explain_fr: « I'm afraid » annonce une mauvaise nouvelle avec tact ; c'est l'adoucisseur britannique par excellence.

gaps.text: With three people away at once, we would be too ___ to cover the helpdesk.
gaps.explain_fr: « Short-staffed » = en sous-effectif. Donner la raison concrète rend le refus plus acceptable.

gaps.text: Would the last two weeks of August ___ for you instead?
gaps.explain_fr: « Would that work for you? » : façon courante et courtoise de proposer une autre solution.

gaps.text: ___, any two weeks in July would be fine.
gaps.explain_fr: « Alternatively » introduit une seconde option en tête de phrase, suivie d'une virgule.

gaps.text: Could you let me ___ by Friday which option you'd prefer?
gaps.explain_fr: « To let someone know » = faire savoir. Bien plus naturel que « to inform me ».

writing.model:
Subject: Your leave request - 4 to 15 August

Hi Lucas,

Thank you for your request for leave from 4 to 15 August.

I'm afraid I can't approve those dates, as Inès and Paul are already off that fortnight. With three people away at once, we would be too short-staffed to cover the helpdesk.

Would the last two weeks of August work for you instead? Alternatively, any two weeks in July would be fine.

Could you let me know by Friday which option you'd prefer? I realise this isn't the answer you were hoping for, and I'll make sure you get first choice next summer.

Best wishes,
Hélène

commentary.quote: I'm afraid I can't approve those dates
commentary.note_fr: Le refus est net mais adouci par « I'm afraid ». On ne dit pas « I refuse your request » : trop brutal.

commentary.quote: as Inès and Paul are already off that fortnight
commentary.note_fr: « As » introduit la cause sans insister. « Fortnight » (quinze jours) est britannique ; un Américain écrirait « those two weeks ».

commentary.quote: Would the last two weeks of August work for you instead?
commentary.note_fr: Le refus est aussitôt suivi d'une proposition : c'est ce qui le rend acceptable.

commentary.quote: I realise this isn't the answer you were hoping for
commentary.note_fr: Reconnaître la déception de l'autre, sans s'excuser à l'excès. Orthographe britannique : « realise ».

commentary.quote: I'll make sure you get first choice next summer
commentary.note_fr: Engagement concret pour l'avenir. « To get first choice » = être prioritaire.

checklist: Have I softened the refusal ('I'm afraid')?
Have I given a concrete reason?
Have I offered at least one alternative?
Have I asked for a reply by a given date?
Is the tone friendly but clear?
phrasebank: I'm afraid I can't approve those dates.
We would be too short-staffed to ...
Would ... work for you instead?
Alternatively, ... would be fine.
Could you let me know by ... which option you'd prefer?
I realise this isn't the answer you were hoping for.

writing.title: Explaining RTT days to a British client
writing.brief: Your British client has noticed 'RTT' on the leave records of his French team and asks what it means. Write one clear paragraph (90-130 words) for a note to him.
writing.brief_fr: Votre client britannique a remarqué la mention « RTT » sur les relevés de congés de son équipe française et vous demande ce qu'elle signifie. Rédigez un paragraphe clair (90 à 130 mots) pour une note à son attention.
outline: What RTT days are, in one sentence
Why they exist: the 35-hour week and longer contractual hours
How they differ from paid holiday
A comparison a British reader will recognise
One practical consequence for him
writing.model: RTT days are additional days off which compensate employees for working more than the statutory 35 hours a week. Your Paris team, for instance, is contracted to work 39 hours; rather than being paid four hours of overtime every week, they earn roughly one day off a month. These days are quite separate from the five weeks of paid holiday to which every employee in France is entitled, and they follow their own rules, which are set out in the company agreement. The closest British parallel is probably time off in lieu. In practice, this means that the days cannot simply be withdrawn if the workload increases: they are owed for hours that have already been worked.

commentary.quote: RTT days are additional days off which compensate employees for working more than the statutory 35 hours a week.
commentary.note_fr: La définition tient en une phrase et ouvre le paragraphe : le lecteur pressé a déjà l'essentiel.

commentary.quote: Your Paris team, for instance, is contracted to work 39 hours
commentary.note_fr: Un exemple tiré de la situation du client vaut mieux qu'une règle abstraite. « To be contracted to work » = avoir un horaire contractuel de.

commentary.quote: These days are quite separate from
commentary.note_fr: « Quite separate » = tout à fait distincts. Ici, « quite » renforce au lieu d'atténuer.

commentary.quote: The closest British parallel is probably time off in lieu.
commentary.note_fr: Comparer avec une notion que le lecteur connaît, en restant prudent grâce à « probably ».

commentary.quote: In practice, this means that
commentary.note_fr: Formule de transition vers la conséquence concrète, qui est ce que le client attend vraiment.

checklist: Does my first sentence define the notion?
Have I given an example from the client's own situation?
Have I distinguished RTT days from paid holiday?
Have I offered a comparison the reader knows?
Have I ended with a practical consequence?

Your team, for instance, is contracted to work ...
These days are quite separate from ...
The closest British parallel is probably ...
In practice, this means that ...
They follow their own rules, which are set out in ...

writing.title: Minuting a discussion on the on-call rota
writing.brief: You took notes at an HR/IT meeting about the on-call rota. Write the paragraph of the minutes recording the discussion and the decisions (90-130 words): four engineers share the rota; complaints about frequency; decision to recruit a fifth volunteer; call-outs to be logged; review in three months.
writing.brief_fr: Vous avez pris des notes lors d'une réunion RH/informatique sur le planning d'astreinte. Rédigez le paragraphe du compte rendu qui retrace la discussion et les décisions (90 à 130 mots) : quatre ingénieurs se partagent l'astreinte ; plaintes sur la fréquence ; décision de recruter un cinquième volontaire ; interventions à consigner ; point dans trois mois.
outline: The item and the current situation
The concern raised and by whom
The legal reminder given by HR
The decisions, with who does what and by when
The follow-up
writing.model:
3. On-call rota

Mr Renaud explained that weekend on-call duty is currently shared between four engineers, each of whom is therefore on call one weekend in four. Two members of the team had reported that this was becoming difficult to sustain. Ms Morel reminded the meeting that time spent on a call-out counts as working time and must not cut into the daily rest period. It was agreed that a fifth volunteer would be sought within the department, so as to reduce the frequency to one weekend in five. With immediate effect, all call-outs are to be logged in the timesheet system. Mr Renaud will report back on both points at the September meeting.

commentary.quote: Mr Renaud explained that weekend on-call duty is currently shared between four engineers
commentary.note_fr: Un compte rendu rapporte les propos au discours indirect, avec des verbes variés : « explained », « reported », « reminded ».

commentary.quote: Two members of the team had reported that this was becoming difficult to sustain.
commentary.note_fr: « Difficult to sustain » : formulation mesurée, sans nommer les intéressés. C'est le ton attendu d'un compte rendu.

commentary.quote: It was agreed that a fifth volunteer would be sought
commentary.note_fr: « It was agreed that » : formule consacrée pour consigner une décision collective. « Sought » est le participe passé de « to seek ».

commentary.quote: With immediate effect, all call-outs are to be logged
commentary.note_fr: « Are to be + participe passé » exprime une obligation décidée en réunion. « To log » = consigner.

commentary.quote: Mr Renaud will report back on both points at the September meeting.
commentary.note_fr: Chaque décision a un responsable et une échéance. « To report back » = rendre compte.

checklist: Have I used reported speech and past tenses consistently?
Is each decision introduced by a clear formula ('It was agreed that')?
Does every action have an owner and a deadline?
Have I kept opinions and adjectives out of the minutes?
Is the item numbered and titled?

Y reminded the meeting that ...
It was agreed that ...
With immediate effect, ... are to be ...
X will report back on ... at the next meeting.
Two members of the team had reported that ...
... so as to reduce the frequency to ...

writing.title: A letter granting unpaid leave
writing.brief: On behalf of the HR Director, write to Ms Garnier, who asked on 3 February for three months of unpaid leave (1 June to 31 August) for a personal project. The company agrees. Set out the conditions: contract suspended, no pay, no accrual of paid leave for the period, return to her current post, and confirmation of her return date in writing by 31 July.
writing.brief_fr: Au nom de la DRH, écrivez à Mme Garnier, qui a demandé le 3 février un congé sans solde de trois mois (du 1er juin au 31 août) pour un projet personnel. L'entreprise accepte. Précisez les conditions : suspension du contrat, absence de rémunération, pas d'acquisition de congés payés sur la période, retour sur son poste actuel, confirmation écrite de sa date de retour avant le 31 juillet.
outline: Reference to her request and the decision
The dates and the effect on her contract and pay
The effect on paid leave and benefits
Her return: post, date, confirmation
Handover before she leaves; good wishes
writing.model:
Dear Ms Garnier,

Your request for unpaid leave

Thank you for your letter of 3 February, in which you asked to take three months' unpaid leave in order to pursue a personal project. I am pleased to confirm that the Company has agreed to your request.

Your leave will run from 1 June to 31 August inclusive. During that time your contract of employment will be suspended: you will not be required to work and you will receive no salary. Please note that the period will not count towards the accrual of paid leave.

You will return to your current position on Monday 1 September, on the same terms as before. I would be grateful if you could confirm your return in writing by 31 July, so that we can plan accordingly.

Before you leave, please agree handover arrangements with your manager, Mr Faure, who will organise cover for your files.

I wish you every success with your project and look forward to welcoming you back in September.

Yours sincerely,

Anne Lefèvre
HR Director
writing.model_us:
Dear Ms. Garnier:

Re: Your request for unpaid leave

Thank you for your letter of February 3, in which you asked to take a three-month unpaid leave of absence to pursue a personal project. I am pleased to confirm that the Company has approved your request.

Your leave will run from June 1 through August 31. During that time your employment contract will be suspended: you will not be required to work and you will receive no salary. Please note that the period will not count toward the accrual of paid leave.

You will return to your current position on Monday, September 1, on the same terms as before. I would appreciate it if you could confirm your return in writing by July 31, so that we can plan accordingly.

Before you leave, please agree on transition arrangements with your manager, Mr. Faure, who will organize coverage for your files.

I wish you every success with your project and look forward to welcoming you back in September.

Sincerely,

Anne Lefèvre
HR Director

commentary.quote: I am pleased to confirm that the Company has agreed to your request.
commentary.note_fr: La décision figure dès le premier paragraphe. « To agree to a request » (accepter une demande), à distinguer de « to agree with someone ».

commentary.quote: three months' unpaid leave
commentary.note_fr: Génitif de durée avec apostrophe après le « s ». La version américaine préfère « a three-month unpaid leave of absence ».

commentary.quote: from 1 June to 31 August inclusive
commentary.note_fr: « Inclusive » lève toute ambiguïté sur le dernier jour ; l'américain dit « from June 1 through August 31 ».

commentary.quote: Please note that the period will not count towards the accrual of paid leave.
commentary.note_fr: « Please note that » introduit un point défavorable sans dramatiser. « To count towards » = être pris en compte pour.

commentary.quote: I would be grateful if you could confirm your return in writing by 31 July
commentary.note_fr: Demande polie de référence, assortie d'une échéance précise et de sa justification.

commentary.quote: look forward to welcoming you back
commentary.note_fr: « To look forward to » est suivi du gérondif : « welcoming », jamais « to welcome ».

checklist: Is the decision stated in the first paragraph?
Are the dates unambiguous ('inclusive', 'by')?
Have I explained the effect on pay and on paid leave?
Have I said what the employee must do, and by when?
Do the salutation and the close match (Dear Ms ... / Yours sincerely)?
Does the letter end on a warm note?
phrasebank: Thank you for your letter of ..., in which you asked to ...
I am pleased to confirm that the Company has agreed to your request.
Your leave will run from ... to ... inclusive.
During that time your contract of employment will be suspended.
Please note that ...
I would be grateful if you could confirm ... in writing by ...
I look forward to welcoming you back in ...

writing.title: A short report on out-of-hours emails
writing.brief: The managing director of a French subsidiary has asked you for a short report (180-230 words) after a staff survey showed that many employees answer emails late in the evening. Set out the findings, the legal position in general terms and three practical recommendations.
writing.brief_fr: Le directeur général d'une filiale française vous demande un court rapport (180 à 230 mots) à la suite d'une enquête interne montrant que de nombreux salariés répondent à leurs courriels tard le soir. Exposez les constats, la situation juridique en termes généraux et trois recommandations pratiques.
outline: Purpose of the report
Findings of the survey
The legal position: right to disconnect, rest periods, the employer's exposure
Three recommendations
Next step
writing.model:
Out-of-hours email: findings and recommendations

1. Purpose
This report summarises the results of the March staff survey on out-of-hours working and proposes three practical measures.

2. Findings
Six out of ten respondents say they regularly answer emails after 8 pm, and nearly a third do so at weekends. Most add that nobody has asked them to; they simply feel it is expected.

3. Legal position
French law recognises a right to disconnect, and the way in which it is exercised must be addressed through company-level negotiation or, failing agreement, a policy drawn up by the employer. More importantly, evening work may cut into the daily rest period of eleven consecutive hours. Should a dispute arise, late-night emails could be relied on as evidence of unpaid overtime or of an excessive workload.

4. Recommendations
First, managers should lead by example and schedule non-urgent emails for the following morning. Second, a short policy should make it clear that no reply is expected outside working hours, save in a genuine emergency. Third, workload should be discussed in one-to-one meetings whenever late working becomes a habit.

5. Next step
I suggest presenting these proposals to the works council at its June meeting.

commentary.quote: This report summarises the results of the March staff survey
commentary.note_fr: Un rapport annonce son objet en une phrase, au présent. Orthographe britannique : « summarises ».

commentary.quote: Six out of ten respondents say they regularly answer emails after 8 pm
commentary.note_fr: Les constats sont chiffrés et attribués (« respondents say »), sans commentaire. « Six out of ten » est plus parlant que « 60% ».

commentary.quote: they simply feel it is expected
commentary.note_fr: Phrase courte après une longue : le rythme met en valeur le constat essentiel.

commentary.quote: Should a dispute arise, late-night emails could be relied on as evidence
commentary.note_fr: Inversion soutenue (« Should a dispute arise » = « If a dispute arises ») et modal prudent « could » : on signale un risque sans l'affirmer.

commentary.quote: First, managers should lead by example
commentary.note_fr: Recommandations numérotées par « First / Second / Third », chacune avec « should ». « To lead by example » = montrer l'exemple.

commentary.quote: save in a genuine emergency
commentary.note_fr: « Save in » = sauf en cas de (registre soutenu). « Genuine » = réel, véritable.

checklist: Does the report have numbered headings?
Are findings kept separate from recommendations?
Have I described the law in general terms, without inventing references?
Is each recommendation concrete and introduced by 'should'?
Have I used cautious language for legal risk ('may', 'could')?
Does the report end with a next step?
phrasebank: This report summarises ... and proposes ...
Six out of ten respondents say ...
French law recognises ...
Should a dispute arise, ... could be relied on as evidence of ...
First, ... Second, ... Third, ...
... save in a genuine emergency.
I suggest presenting these proposals to ...

dialogues.title: Three requests for the same fortnight
dialogues.context: Hannah, a team leader in the London office of a Franco-British firm, calls Claire, the HR consultant, about clashing summer leave requests in her Paris team.
dialogues.context_fr: Hannah, responsable d'équipe au bureau londonien d'un cabinet franco-britannique, appelle Claire, consultante RH, au sujet de demandes de congés d'été concurrentes dans son équipe parisienne.

lines.speaker: Hannah
lines.text: Claire, have you got a minute? I've got a bit of a headache with the summer rota.
lines.note_fr: « Have you got a minute? » : entrée en matière britannique courante. « A bit of a headache » = un petit casse-tête (understatement).

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Of course. What's the problem?

lines.speaker: Hannah
lines.text: Three of the Paris team have all put in for the first fortnight of August, and I can't possibly let them all go at once.
lines.note_fr: « To put in for » = déposer une demande de. « Fortnight » = quinze jours (UK uniquement).

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: No, you can't. How many do you need in to keep things ticking over?
lines.note_fr: « To keep things ticking over » = assurer le service minimum, faire tourner la boutique.

lines.speaker: Hannah
lines.text: Two at the very least. In London I'd just go on first come, first served. Is that all right in France?
lines.note_fr: « First come, first served » = premier arrivé, premier servi.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Not quite, I'm afraid. In France it's the employer who sets the order of leave, and you're expected to take things like family circumstances and length of service into account.
lines.note_fr: « Not quite, I'm afraid » : contredire en douceur. « To take into account » = tenir compte de.

lines.speaker: Hannah
lines.text: So the one with school-age children gets priority?

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: It certainly weighs in her favour. I'd also look at who had August last year. And whatever you decide, do tell them soon, because once the dates are fixed you can't easily change them close to departure.
lines.note_fr: « To weigh in someone's favour » = jouer en faveur de quelqu'un. « Do tell them » : le « do » d'insistance, poli et ferme.

lines.speaker: Hannah
lines.text: Right. So I say yes to Samira, and ask the other two to sort it out between them?
lines.note_fr: « To sort it out between them » = s'arranger entre eux.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: I'd give them the chance, yes, with a deadline. If they can't agree by Friday, you decide, and you explain why.

lines.speaker: Hannah
lines.text: That sounds fair. Could you send me a couple of lines on the criteria, so I've got something to point to?
lines.note_fr: « Something to point to » = un élément sur lequel s'appuyer.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Will do. You'll have it by the end of the day.
lines.note_fr: « Will do » : réponse brève et courante pour « je m'en occupe ».

questions.q: What is Hannah's problem?
options: Nobody wants to take leave in August
Three people want the same two weeks and she needs two at work
The Paris office closes in August
She has lost the leave requests
questions.explain_fr: Trois personnes ont demandé la même quinzaine (« fortnight ») alors qu'il en faut au moins deux présentes.

questions.q: According to Claire, how is priority decided in France?
options: Strictly first come, first served
By drawing lots
By a vote within the team
By the employer, having regard to criteria such as family circumstances and length of service
questions.explain_fr: C'est l'employeur qui fixe l'ordre des départs, en tenant compte notamment de la situation de famille et de l'ancienneté.

questions.q: What does Claire advise Hannah to do about the other two employees?
options: Let them try to agree by a deadline, then decide herself
Refuse both requests
Approve both and hire a temp
Ask the London team to cover
questions.explain_fr: Leur laisser une chance de s'entendre, avec une échéance (« by Friday »), puis trancher en expliquant sa décision.

dialogues.title: Why can't they just be on call?
dialogues.context: A video call between Brad, Director of Engineering at a US software company, and Claire, a French HR consultant. Brad wants his three engineers in Nantes to join the global weekend on-call rotation.
dialogues.context_fr: Visioconférence entre Brad, directeur de l'ingénierie d'un éditeur de logiciels américain, et Claire, consultante RH française. Brad souhaite intégrer ses trois ingénieurs nantais à la rotation mondiale d'astreinte du week-end.

lines.speaker: Brad
lines.text: Hi Claire. Quick one: I need the Nantes guys in the weekend on-call rotation starting next month. Any issues?
lines.note_fr: « Quick one » = une question rapide. « Rotation » : terme américain pour le roulement d'astreinte (UK : « rota »).

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: It's doable, but not quite as simple as adding their names to the schedule. Can I walk you through the three things that matter?
lines.note_fr: « It's doable, but » : dire oui tout en annonçant des réserves. « To walk someone through » = expliquer pas à pas.

lines.speaker: Brad
lines.text: Sure, go ahead.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: First, on-call has to be set up properly: either through a collective agreement or, if there isn't one, by the employer after consulting the employee representatives.

lines.speaker: Brad
lines.text: Okay. And they're salaried, so I'm assuming there's no extra pay involved?
lines.note_fr: « Salaried » : aux États-Unis, sous-entend « exempt », donc sans heures supplémentaires.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: That's the second point. In France, just being on call has to be compensated, either in money or in time off, even if the phone never rings.
lines.note_fr: « Even if the phone never rings » : image simple pour faire comprendre que l'astreinte seule ouvre droit à compensation.

lines.speaker: Brad
lines.text: Huh. And if it does ring?
lines.note_fr: « Huh » marque la surprise, sans hostilité.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Then the time they spend fixing the problem counts as working time. Which brings me to the third point: rest. If someone's up at 3 a.m. on an incident, you can't expect them at their desk at nine.
lines.note_fr: « Which brings me to » : transition orale efficace. « To be up » = être debout, réveillé.

lines.speaker: Brad
lines.text: So I'd need more people in the rotation to make that work.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Probably, yes. With three engineers, each of them would be on call every third weekend, and that's a lot. I'd look at sharing weekends with another European site.
lines.note_fr: « Every third weekend » = un week-end sur trois. « I'd look at » : suggérer sans imposer.

lines.speaker: Brad
lines.text: Got it. Can you put together a one-pager with the options and the cost?
lines.note_fr: « One-pager » = note d'une page. « To put together » = préparer.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Absolutely. I'll get it to you by Wednesday.

questions.q: What does Claire say about on-call time when nobody calls?
options: It is free for the employer
It counts fully as working time
It must still be compensated, in money or in time off
It is forbidden at weekends
questions.explain_fr: L'astreinte elle-même donne lieu à compensation, financière ou en repos, même sans intervention ; seule l'intervention est du temps de travail effectif.

questions.q: Why is rest an issue?
options: An engineer who worked during the night cannot be expected at work first thing in the morning
French engineers do not work on Mondays
On-call employees get an extra week of vacation
The US office is in a different time zone
questions.explain_fr: L'intervention ne doit pas priver le salarié de son repos quotidien : après un incident à 3 heures, pas de reprise à 9 heures.

questions.q: What does Claire suggest?
options: Paying the engineers a higher salary instead
Sharing weekends with another European site
Cancelling on-call in France
Hiring contractors in the US
questions.explain_fr: Avec trois ingénieurs, un week-end sur trois est trop fréquent : elle propose de mutualiser avec un autre site européen.

dialogues.title: Days, not hours
dialogues.context: Oliver, HR Director of a British group, is reviewing the contracts of the French managers with Claire. He has just come across the 'forfait jours'.
dialogues.context_fr: Oliver, DRH d'un groupe britannique, passe en revue avec Claire les contrats des cadres français. Il vient de découvrir le forfait jours.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: I've been reading the French managers' contracts, and I must say I'm slightly puzzled. There are no working hours in them at all.
lines.note_fr: « I must say I'm slightly puzzled » : understatement britannique pour « je ne comprends pas ».

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: That's deliberate. They're on what we call an annual working-days arrangement: their time is counted in days per year, not in hours.
lines.note_fr: « What we call » introduit le terme technique avant de l'expliquer.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: So no overtime, however late they stay?

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: No overtime, that's right. But it isn't a blank cheque. They still have to get their daily and weekly rest, and the company has to keep an eye on their workload.
lines.note_fr: « It isn't a blank cheque » = ce n'est pas un chèque en blanc. « To keep an eye on » = surveiller.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: I see. It sounds rather like our opt-out from the 48-hour week.
lines.note_fr: « Rather like » = assez proche de.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: I can see why you'd say that, but it works quite differently. The opt-out is an individual choice. Here you need a collective agreement first, and then each manager's written consent.
lines.note_fr: « I can see why you'd say that, but » : nuancer une comparaison sans froisser.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: And what happens if we don't do the monitoring? In practice, I mean.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Then the arrangement may not stand up in court. The manager could go back to the 35-hour rules and claim overtime for the hours actually worked.
lines.note_fr: « To stand up in court » = tenir devant un juge. « May » et « could » : on signale un risque sans l'affirmer.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: Goodness. That could add up.
lines.note_fr: « That could add up » = l'addition pourrait être lourde (encore un understatement).

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: It could. Which is why I'd like to check two things: that the annual workload meetings are actually taking place, and that there's a written record of them.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: I rather suspect they aren't. Shall we start with the sales directors?
lines.note_fr: « I rather suspect » : façon très britannique d'exprimer une quasi-certitude.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Good idea. I'll draw up a simple checklist and we can go through it on Monday.
lines.note_fr: « To draw up » = établir (un document). « To go through » = passer en revue.

questions.q: Why are there no working hours in the managers' contracts?
options: The contracts are incomplete
French managers have no limits on their working time
Their time is counted in days per year
They are paid by the hour
questions.explain_fr: Ils relèvent du forfait jours : le temps de travail est décompté en jours sur l'année, et non en heures.

questions.q: How does the arrangement differ from the British opt-out, according to Claire?
options: It requires a collective agreement as well as individual consent
It needs no consent at all
It only applies to part-time staff
It can be ended by the employee at any time
questions.explain_fr: L'« opt-out » britannique est un choix individuel ; le forfait jours suppose d'abord un accord collectif, puis l'accord écrit du salarié.

questions.q: What is the risk if workload is not monitored?
options: The managers lose their rest days
The company must close the French office
The managers become part-time
The arrangement may fail in court and overtime may be claimed
questions.explain_fr: Sans suivi effectif de la charge de travail, la convention de forfait peut être privée d'effet et le salarié réclamer des heures supplémentaires.

dialogues.title: Unlimited PTO, French style
dialogues.context: Megan, Head of People at a San Francisco start-up, wants to extend the company's 'unlimited PTO' policy to its new French employees. She calls Claire.
dialogues.context_fr: Megan, responsable RH d'une start-up de San Francisco, veut étendre la politique de « congés illimités » de l'entreprise à ses nouveaux salariés français. Elle appelle Claire.

lines.speaker: Megan
lines.text: So, we're rolling out unlimited PTO globally, and I'd love to have France on board. People take what they need, and nobody tracks anything.
lines.note_fr: « PTO » (paid time off) : compteur unique de congés aux États-Unis. « To roll out » = déployer. « On board » = partie prenante.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: I like the idea behind it. The part that worries me is 'nobody tracks anything.'
lines.note_fr: Commencer par ce que l'on approuve avant d'exprimer une réserve.

lines.speaker: Megan
lines.text: Why's that? It's more generous than any fixed number.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: It may be, but in France paid vacation isn't just a perk. Employees earn a legal minimum of five weeks a year, and the employer has to be able to show they actually took it.
lines.note_fr: « It may be, but » : concéder avant d'objecter. « Perk » = avantage (familier).

lines.speaker: Megan
lines.text: So we'd still need to count days.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: You would. And honestly, that protects you. With unlimited plans, people often end up taking less time off, not more.
lines.note_fr: « And honestly » introduit un argument de bon sens à l'oral. « To end up doing » = finir par faire.

lines.speaker: Megan
lines.text: Yeah, we've seen that here too. Okay, what would a French version look like?

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Keep the statutory five weeks as a floor, track them properly, and offer extra days on top as your 'flexible' leave. That way you keep the spirit of the policy and stay compliant.
lines.note_fr: « As a floor » = comme plancher. « On top » = en plus. « To stay compliant » = rester en conformité.

lines.speaker: Megan
lines.text: That works. Do the extra days need to go in the contract?

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: I'd put them in a policy rather than in the contract, so you can adjust them later. But let's make sure the wording is clear about which days are which.
lines.note_fr: « Which days are which » = quels jours relèvent de quelle catégorie.

lines.speaker: Megan
lines.text: Makes sense. Can you draft something for me to run by legal?
lines.note_fr: « To run something by someone » = soumettre quelque chose à quelqu'un pour avis. « Legal » = le service juridique.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Sure. I'll have a draft with you early next week.

questions.q: What worries Claire about the unlimited PTO policy?
options: It is too generous
That nobody would keep track of leave taken
It would cost too much
French employees dislike vacation
questions.explain_fr: Le problème n'est pas la générosité mais l'absence de suivi : l'employeur français doit pouvoir justifier que les congés légaux ont bien été pris.

questions.q: What does Claire say often happens under unlimited plans?
options: People take all of August off
Managers refuse every request
People sue their employer
People take less time off
questions.explain_fr: « People often end up taking less time off, not more » : faute de repère, les salariés prennent souvent moins de congés.

questions.q: What solution does Claire propose?
options: Keep and track the statutory five weeks, and add flexible days on top
Apply the US policy unchanged
Pay employees instead of giving leave
Give French staff no extra days
questions.explain_fr: Les cinq semaines légales servent de plancher (« floor ») et sont décomptées ; les jours supplémentaires « flexibles » figurent dans une politique interne.

roleplays.title: The 35-hour week for a sceptical CFO
roleplays.situation: You are on a call with Greg, the CFO of a US group that has just bought a French company. He has heard that 'the French only work 35 hours' and wants to understand what overtime will cost him. Explain the rules simply and correct his assumptions.
roleplays.situation_fr: Vous êtes en visioconférence avec Greg, directeur financier d'un groupe américain qui vient de racheter une société française. Il a entendu dire que « les Français ne travaillent que 35 heures » et veut comprendre ce que les heures supplémentaires vont lui coûter. Expliquez simplement les règles et corrigez ses idées reçues.

turns.say: So help me out here. Is it true your people aren't allowed to work more than 35 hours a week?
turns.model: That's a very common misunderstanding. Thirty-five hours isn't a cap: it's simply the point at which overtime starts. Plenty of people in France work 39 or 40 hours a week, and that's perfectly lawful.
turns.tips_fr: Corrigez sans vexer : « That's a very common misunderstanding ». Opposez clairement « cap » (plafond) et « the point at which overtime starts » (seuil).

turns.say: Okay. So anything over 35 is overtime, even for my managers?
turns.model: For most employees, yes. The exception is senior, autonomous staff whose time is counted in days per year rather than hours; they don't get overtime. It's a bit like exempt status in the US, but it has to be set up through a collective agreement and the employee has to consent in writing.
turns.tips_fr: Utilisez le repère américain « exempt status », puis nuancez aussitôt par « but ». Restez général : ni chiffres ni références.

turns.say: And the others - can't they just agree to waive overtime? We pay well.
turns.model: I'm afraid not. Overtime rights can't be waived, even in a signed contract. What you can do is replace part of the pay with time off, if the collective agreement allows it.
turns.tips_fr: Refus net mais poli (« I'm afraid not »), suivi d'une ouverture : « What you can do is... ».

turns.say: Is there any limit, or can I ask for as much overtime as I'm willing to pay for?
turns.model: There are limits. There are maximum daily and weekly hours, and minimum rest periods between working days. On top of that, each employee has a yearly overtime quota; once you go beyond it, you owe extra rest as well as pay. So heavy, regular overtime becomes expensive quite quickly.
turns.tips_fr: Structurez : plafonds, repos, contingent. « On top of that » relie naturellement les points. Terminez par la conséquence financière, qui intéresse un directeur financier.

turns.say: Got it. What's the one thing I should do first?
turns.model: Make sure hours are recorded reliably. If someone ever claims unpaid overtime, the court will ask the company for its records, so good timekeeping is your best protection. I'd be happy to review the current system with your HR team.
turns.tips_fr: Une seule recommandation, comme demandé. « Timekeeping » est le mot américain pour le décompte des heures. Finissez par une offre concrète.

roleplays.title: A request to go down to four days
roleplays.situation: You are the HR manager. Emma, a project manager returning from maternity leave next month, comes to see you. She would like to work four days a week. Listen, explain how the request will be handled, and agree on next steps.
roleplays.situation_fr: Vous êtes responsable RH. Emma, chef de projet qui reprend le mois prochain après son congé de maternité, vient vous voir. Elle souhaite travailler quatre jours par semaine. Écoutez-la, expliquez comment sa demande sera traitée et convenez des prochaines étapes.

turns.say: Thanks for seeing me. I'm due back on the 3rd, and I've been wondering whether I could come back four days a week.
turns.model: Of course, and thank you for raising it before your return rather than after. It gives us time to plan. Could you tell me a bit more about what you have in mind - which day you'd like off, and for how long?
turns.tips_fr: Accueillez la demande positivement, puis posez des questions ouvertes. « What you have in mind » = ce que vous envisagez.

turns.say: Ideally Wednesdays, at least until my daughter starts school. Would I lose my job as project manager?
turns.model: No, you'd keep your role; only your hours and your pay would change, in proportion. As it's linked to your child, you may be able to take it as part-time parental leave, which gives you a right to go back to full-time afterwards. Otherwise it would be an ordinary amendment to your contract.
turns.tips_fr: Rassurez d'abord (« No, you'd keep your role »), puis distinguez les deux voies : congé parental à temps partiel ou avenant classique.

turns.say: That's a relief. My worry is that I'll still have five days' work to do in four.
turns.model: That's a fair concern, and it's exactly what we need to avoid. If you move to four days, your workload has to be adjusted accordingly. I'd suggest sitting down with your manager to decide which projects are handed over.
turns.tips_fr: « That's a fair concern » valide l'inquiétude. « Accordingly » = en conséquence. « To hand over » = transférer (des dossiers).

turns.say: OK. And do I need to do anything formal?
turns.model: Yes, please put the request in writing: the pattern you'd like, the start date and how long you'd want it to last. Once I have that, I'll speak to your manager and come back to you within two weeks.
turns.tips_fr: Soyez précis sur la démarche et le délai. « To put something in writing » = formuler par écrit ; « to come back to you » = revenir vers vous.

roleplays.title: Emails at eleven at night
roleplays.situation: You are the HR business partner. Several members of David's team have told you, in confidence, that he sends emails late at night and expects answers by morning. David is a high-performing British manager based in Paris. Raise the subject with him tactfully.
roleplays.situation_fr: Vous êtes HR business partner. Plusieurs membres de l'équipe de David vous ont confié qu'il envoie des courriels tard le soir et attend des réponses pour le lendemain matin. David est un manager britannique performant, en poste à Paris. Abordez le sujet avec tact.

turns.say: You wanted a word? I've got about ten minutes before my next call.
turns.model: Thanks, David, ten minutes is plenty. I wanted to talk about something that's come up in the team: emails sent late in the evening. It's not a complaint as such, but a few people feel they're expected to reply the same night.
turns.tips_fr: Entrez vite dans le sujet, en dédramatisant : « It's not a complaint as such ». Ne citez personne.

turns.say: Really? I never ask anyone to reply. I just clear my inbox when the kids are in bed.
turns.model: I don't doubt that for a moment, and working in the evening is entirely your choice. The trouble is that when an email comes from the boss at eleven, people tend to feel they ought to answer it, whatever you intended.
turns.tips_fr: Reconnaissez sa bonne foi (« I don't doubt that for a moment ») avant d'exposer l'effet produit. « The trouble is that » introduit le problème sans accuser.

turns.say: Fair point, I suppose. But is it really an HR matter?
turns.model: It is, actually. In France employees have a right to disconnect, and they're entitled to eleven hours' rest between two working days. If someone is answering at midnight and back at eight, we have a problem, and those emails would be the evidence.
turns.tips_fr: « It is, actually » : contredire poliment. Expliquez la règle en une phrase, puis le risque concret.

turns.say: I hadn't thought of it that way. What would you like me to do?
turns.model: Two small things would make a real difference. Use the delayed-send option so that emails go out in the morning, and tell the team clearly that nothing sent after hours needs an answer before the next day. Would you be comfortable with that?
turns.tips_fr: Proposez deux gestes simples et terminez par une question qui l'associe à la solution : « Would you be comfortable with that? ».

roleplays.title: Explaining remote work rules to a new US manager
roleplays.situation: Kelly has just arrived from Chicago to run a team of eight in Lyon. She wants everyone back in the office five days a week from next Monday. The team currently works from home two days a week under a company policy. Explain what she can and cannot do.
roleplays.situation_fr: Kelly vient d'arriver de Chicago pour diriger une équipe de huit personnes à Lyon. Elle veut que tout le monde revienne au bureau cinq jours par semaine dès lundi prochain. L'équipe télétravaille actuellement deux jours par semaine en application d'une charte d'entreprise. Expliquez-lui ce qu'elle peut faire et ne pas faire.

turns.say: I want the whole team in the office full-time, starting Monday. I can't build a team over video calls.
turns.model: I understand why you'd want that as a new manager. I'd advise against doing it from Monday, though. The team works from home under a formal company policy, and that policy sets out how the arrangement can be changed or ended.
turns.tips_fr: Validez l'objectif, puis freinez : « I'd advise against..., though ». Le « though » final adoucit l'objection à l'oral.

turns.say: A policy is just a policy. Back home I'd simply announce it.
turns.model: Here it carries more weight than that. Remote work is agreed between the employer and each employee, and ending it normally means following the notice period and the procedure the policy lays down. If you skip that, people can legitimately push back.
turns.tips_fr: « It carries more weight » = cela a plus de portée. « To push back » = s'y opposer, contester (courant en anglais américain des affaires).

turns.say: So what are my options? I'm not waiting six months.
turns.model: You won't have to. In the short term you can use the flexibility the policy already gives you: for example, fix one or two days when everyone has to be on site. Then, if you still want to change the rules, we consult the employee representatives and give proper notice.
turns.tips_fr: Répondez à l'impatience par une solution immédiate, puis par la voie formelle. « In the short term... Then... » structure la réponse.

turns.say: All right, two team days a week I can live with. How do we announce it?
turns.model: I'd keep it simple: explain at your next team meeting why you want those days together, and confirm it by email with a start date a couple of weeks out. I can draft the message for you if that helps.
turns.tips_fr: « I'd keep it simple » annonce un conseil pratique. « A couple of weeks out » (US) = dans une quinzaine de jours. Terminez par une offre d'aide.
